title: observability: propagate request_id/trace through streaming & function-calls, structured logs, per-endpoint metrics tags (OpenAI-compat)
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Improve observability across the public API surface (text generation, chat streaming, function/tool calls, and OpenAI-compat layer) by consistently propagating request IDs and trace headers, enriching structured logs with contextual fields, and tagging per-endpoint metrics so dashboards/alerts can attribute traffic/cost/latency correctly. This change addresses gaps found during incident INC-2026-02 (streaming connection attribution) and follows ENG-2345 and ENG-2389 work items.

Summary of changes: - Propagate X-Request-Id and W3C traceparent/tracecontext headers from API gateway through the entire request path (router -> handlers -> serving runtime -> streaming multiplex). - Ensure stream chunk events include request_id and trace_id in the JSON wire format used by the OpenAI-compat streaming layer. - Add contextual structured fields to logs emitted from API handlers and stream encoders (request_id, trace_id, client_suborg, route_name, model_variant). - Attach per-endpoint metric tags (route_name, method, openai_compat=true/false) to the existing latency/cost/counter metrics so they appear on per-route dashboards. - Update OpenAI-compat translation layer to preserve incoming trace headers and include them in the compat response metadata (for customers bridging from OpenAI tooling). - Small SDK/console docs update describing new top-level log fields and metrics tags.

Implementation notes: - Request ID generation: gateway will still prefer incoming X-Request-Id; if missing we synthesize a UUIDv4 at edge. All internal calls carry X-Request-Id and traceparent. - Streaming compatibility: stream framing kept unchanged for non-OpenAI clients; for Close-to-OpenAI streaming we include a top-level metadata event at stream start containing request_id and trace_id to avoid changing every chunk. For internal consumers we also emit per-chunk context fields to aid debugging. - Metrics tagging implemented by adding a lightweight route_name tag to the metric label set in the handler middleware (zero-cost no-ops when aggregation disabled). Uses existing metrics library tagging primitives to avoid cardinality explosion. - Backwards compatibility: no breaking change to API format for standard clients; OpenAI-compat layer will include a single initial metadata event when streaming and an equivalent field in non-streaming responses.

Testing and rollout: - Unit tests for header propagation and structured log fields added. Integration tests added to perf-canary to validate tags show up in metric aggregation and dashboard snapshots. End-to-end scenario included for function-calls and streaming in redwood-e2e harness. - Canary rollout: enabled by feature flag observability.request_propagation on 10% of traffic for 24h, monitor error budget, stream reconnection rate, and metric cardinality. Gradual 100% rollout after 48h if no regressions.

Checklist:
- [x] Header propagation middleware implementation
- [x] Streaming metadata event and chunk tagging
- [x] OpenAI-compat translation updates
- [x] Structured log fields added and documented
- [x] Per-endpoint metric tags implemented and validated in canary
- [x] Unit/integration tests and perf canary runs

Related: Linear ENG-2345, ENG-2389, PM-442. Jira SUP-338 for customer incident follow-up.

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Left a few nits around the middleware layering. Can we ensure the middleware is idempotent when called twice in an edge case?
Asha Patel: Good catch — middleware now guards against double-instrumentation by checking existing X-Request-Id and a propagated flag.
Lena Cho: Verified that the initial streaming metadata event does not break existing clients in our integration tests. Approving with minor doc suggestion.
Ravi Srinivasan: Confirmed metric tags are low cardinality on the canary rollouts. Approve.
release_notes:
- Added propagation of request_id and W3C trace headers through API and streaming paths.
- Streaming start metadata includes request_id/trace for OpenAI-compat flows.
- Structured logs now include request_id, trace_id, route_name, and model_variant.
- Per-endpoint metric tags (route_name, method, openai_compat) for more granular dashboards.
